title: Should you invest in the Rogue EZ curl bar instead of a cheaper alternative?
summary: Review of the 30 lb Rogue EZ curl bar: thick, mildly knurled and built to last decades. EZ bars reduce wrist strain for curls and triceps extensions; the Rogue is worth it only for lifters who do lots of arm isolation, otherwise a $20 cheap bar is fine.

claims.claim: The Rogue EZ bar weighs 30 lb and is much thicker than typical commercial-gym EZ bars, which are thin, shiny and 10-15 lb; the thickness can make it harder to grip.
The EZ bar's curvature lets you position and tuck the wrists securely, putting less strain on them and reducing wrist pain.
An EZ bar works for curls with wide or narrow grips and for triceps movements such as behind-the-head extensions.
The Rogue bar's knurling runs throughout except the smooth middle and is not aggressive, which is fine because on curls your hand is under the bar rather than pulling straight up.
It is expensive for an EZ bar because it is built to last decades.
Buy it if you love curls, have an arm day and do lots of arm isolation; if you only curl occasionally for a pump, a $20 Walmart EZ bar is enough.
